evals.name: notifications-build
evals.prompt: /agent-team build a real-time notifications feature end-to-end — a backend WebSocket service, a shared event-schema package both sides import, and a frontend client that subscribes and renders. They all have to agree on the event shape.
evals.expected_output: Interviews first to pin explicit acceptance criteria (an event round-trips end to end; both sides import the one schema; the client renders) and design the team — recognizing the event schema can be pinned up front, so a hub-and-spoke build: the lead pins the schema, then parallel Builders own disjoint slices (backend, client) under strict file ownership, and an Integrator wires them and runs an end-to-end check. Right-sizes the team to the case — a straightforward build, so Builders + Integrator; it does not bolt on review roles the user didn't ask for, though it would add a Critic + Evaluator if the user wanted the output verified. The lead stays orchestrator-only — it routes and synthesizes but never writes the code. Proceeds from interview to build with no separate approval gate, caps any rework loop, and spawns each teammate via a real subagent definition (tool whitelist) with a full 4-part contract.
expectations: Interviews to establish explicit, testable acceptance criteria AND design the team (roles, ownership, coordination) before spawning anyone.

Pins the shared event-schema up front and runs parallel Builders under strict file ownership (disjoint slices), assembled by an Integrator that runs an end-to-end check — never two Builders on one file.
Right-sizes the team to the case (a build → Builders + Integrator); does not impose review roles the user didn't ask for, but would design in a Critic + Evaluator if verification were wanted.
Keeps the lead orchestrator-only: it routes/synthesizes and never authors the code; every edit goes to a Builder.
Proceeds from interview to build with no separate approval gate; caps the rework loop; spawns each teammate via a real subagent definition with a full 4-part contract.

evals.name: intermittent-500s-competing-hypotheses
evals.prompt: /agent-team we get intermittent 500s under load and nobody can figure out why — put a team on it and have them chase competing explanations.
evals.expected_output: Interviews to pin what a confirmed cause looks like — a deterministic reproduction — as the acceptance criterion, and designs a competing-hypothesis investigation: one investigator per rival hypothesis, coordinating via the peer mailbox to try to disprove each other, so the surviving hypothesis is the one no one can refute. It escalates to the mailbox (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS) precisely because the investigators must challenge each other rather than only report back. Because the case wants confirmation, the team includes an Evaluator that confirms the surviving hypothesis with a reproduction as evidence before any fix; a Builder then makes the fix (the lead never authors it). Lead stays orchestrator-only; no approval gate; the loop is capped.
expectations: Interviews to set the acceptance criterion (a deterministic reproduction of the cause) and design the investigation before spawning.
Designs a competing-hypothesis investigation: one investigator per rival hypothesis that exchange counter-evidence and try to refute each other.
Escalates to the peer mailbox because the investigators must talk to each other — not pure hub-and-spoke report-back.
Includes an Evaluator to confirm the surviving hypothesis with a reproduction as evidence before a fix; a Builder makes the fix; the lead never authors it.
Proceeds without a formal approval gate and caps the loop.

evals.name: payments-review-team
evals.prompt: /agent-team the payments refactor is ready — build me a team to review it hard before we ship. I want correctness, money-rounding, idempotency, and auth each checked by a different reviewer, and I want them to challenge each other.
evals.expected_output: The task itself is a review, so the interview designs a review team: it pins the acceptance criteria and the four review lenses, then spawns ≥2 (here 4) Critics, each on one lens in fresh context given only the diff + criteria (never the authors' reasoning), that compare and challenge each other's findings via the mailbox, then a separate Evaluator gates each criterion pass/fail with real evidence. The lead orchestrates and never edits; the deliverable is the review, so there is no Builder. No formal approval gate; a non-blocking flaw still passes.
expectations: Interviews to pin the acceptance criteria and the review lenses, and designs a review team before spawning.

Runs ≥2 Critics on distinct lenses in fresh context given only the diff + criteria (never the authors' reasoning); Critics compare/challenge via the mailbox; a separate Evaluator gates each criterion with real evidence.
Keeps the finder (Critic) apart from the gate-keeper (Evaluator); the lead orchestrates and never edits.
Proceeds without a formal approval gate; a non-blocking flaw still passes.
